econ.label: Sinamalé Bridge: a Chinese-financed cross-sea bridge, opened 2018 at about US$210m
econ.text: The China–Maldives Friendship Bridge, now the Sinamalé Bridge, links Malé with Hulhulé, the airport island. It is 2,000 m long and opened in 2018. A Chinese government grant and a China Eximbank concessional loan financed about US$210m of the cost, and a Chinese state contractor built it. The loan was restructured under the G20 debt-service suspension in 2020.
econ.source: AidData (China's financing record); Wikipedia (Sinamalé Bridge, May 2026); CSIS AMTI (2018)

econ.label: Velana airport expansion: a Chinese contractor; 3,400 m runway, fuel farm and cargo terminal (2018)
econ.text: A Beijing-based contractor, Beijing Urban Construction Group, signed the 2014 deal to expand Velana International Airport. A new 3,400 m runway opened in 2018, with a new fuel farm and a cargo terminal. The analysts at CSIS's AMTI count it among China's largest and most visible projects in the Maldives.
econ.source: CSIS AMTI (2018): Chinese Investment in the Maldives

econ.label: China–Maldives free-trade agreement in force from 1 January 2025 (the Maldives' first FTA)
econ.text: The China–Maldives free-trade agreement, the Maldives' first free-trade agreement, took effect on 1 January 2025.

econ.label: Chinese debt: about US$1.3bn owed to China in 2024; the exact figure is disputed
econ.text: As of 2024 the Maldives owed about US$1.3bn to China, the largest share of its external debt. Maldivian officials have said they struggle to establish the exact amount, and they have sought to renegotiate interest rates and repayment plans.
econ.source: Wikipedia (China–Maldives relations, 2026); Maldivian officials as reported (2024)

econ.label: K. Funadhoo fuel storage: relocation to Maagiri Falhu announced in 2023; status not verified
econ.text: The government announced in 2023 that the fuel storage at K. Funadhoo in Kaafu Atoll would be relocated to Maagiri Falhu, near Thilafushi. The move was announced at the Velana expansion inauguration. Its 2026 status is not verified in this build.

econ.label: Energy: about 600 MW of capacity, 68.5 MW of it solar; the inhabited islands run mostly on diesel
econ.text: In the 2024 energy roadmap, the Maldives had about 600 MW of total generation capacity, of which 68.5 MW was solar PV; solar produced about 6% of electricity. The inhabited islands had about 208 MW at the end of 2023, of which 181 MW was diesel.

econ.label: Thilafushi waste-to-energy: 13 MW planned, at the permitting stage; construction 2026, operation 2027
econ.text: A 13 MW waste-to-energy plant planned at Thilafushi was at the permitting stage. Construction was expected in 2026 and commercial operation in 2027. The plant is not verified as built.

econ.label: Malé-region water supply: about 49,900 tonnes a day; storage about 50,445 tonnes
econ.text: The Malé-region water system produces about 49,900 tonnes of water a day, with storage of about 50,445 tonnes after a new 10,000-tonne tank at Hulhumalé.

econ.label: Hulhumalé Phase II housing: Chinese engagement reported, not verified in this build
econ.text: NUS ISAS reports that China was engaged in the Hulhumalé Phase II housing project, alongside the Velana expansion. The engagement is reported and is not verified in this build.

geo.label: President Muizzu's visit to China (January 2024): 20 agreements and about US$130m in aid
geo.text: President Mohamed Muizzu visited China in January 2024. The visit produced 20 agreements and about US$130m in aid.

geo.label: Makunudhoo: a planned Chinese–Maldivian ocean observation station (2017; reported scrapped; not verified)
geo.text: A 2017 protocol between China's State Oceanic Administration and the Maldives' environment ministry planned a Joint Ocean Observation Station on Makunudhoo, the westernmost inhabited island. Reports say the plan was scrapped; Wikipedia gives 2019. China's foreign ministry said its marine cooperation with the Maldives had no military purpose. The status is not verified in this build.

scs.label: Chinese research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 03: port calls at Malé and Thilafushi (February 2024)
scs.text: The research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 03, owned by a research institute under China's natural resources ministry, was given permission in January 2024 for a port call for rotation of personnel and replenishment. It docked at Malé and then at Thilafushi on 23 February 2024. The government said the ship would not do research in Maldivian waters. Before arriving, the ship had spent weeks surveying waters just outside the exclusive economic zones of neighbouring states.
scs.source: SCMP (2024); Reuters via Malay Mail (22 Feb 2024); Maldivian foreign ministry statement (Jan 2024)

scs.label: Exclusive economic zone of about 900,000 km², the area the Coast Guard and the Air Corps monitor
scs.text: The Maldives' exclusive economic zone covers about 900,000 km², which the Coast Guard and the Air Corps are tasked to monitor.

scs.label: Malé Commercial Harbour and its relocation to Thilafushi (quay-wall work targeted July 2026)
scs.text: Maldives Ports Limited is the sole port authority and runs Malé Commercial Harbour. Under a government project, commercial port operations are being moved to Thilafushi, on about 60 ha, with the quay-wall work targeted to start in July 2026. The project is debt-financed; the source does not name the lender.
scs.source: Ministry of Economic Development, Transport and Trade (Aug 2026); Wikipedia (Maldives Ports Limited)

scs.label: SEA-ME-WE 6 cable landing at Hulhumalé Phase II (Dhiraagu; inaugurated 1 August 2024)
scs.text: Dhiraagu inaugurated the SEA-ME-WE 6 cable landing at Hulhumalé Phase II on 1 August 2024. The 19,200 km cable has a minimum capacity of 100 Tbps. Dhiraagu is the first Maldivian co-owner in a consortium of 16 partners. Full service was expected in early 2026; the go-live is not verified in this build.

scs.label: Eight Degree Channel: sea passage at the northern edge of the archipelago (general navigation; not verified)
scs.text: The Eight Degree Channel is a sea passage named for its latitude, at the northern edge of the archipelago. It is a general navigation reference, not verified in this build.
scs.source: Public information (not verified in this build)

milops.label: MNDF headquarters at Bandaarakoshi, Malé; Chief of Defence Force Ibrahim Hilmy; Minister Hassan Rasheed (since 15 April 2026)
milops.text: The Maldives National Defence Force has its headquarters at Bandaarakoshi, Ameer Ahmed Magu, Malé. The Chief of Defence Force is Major General Ibrahim Hilmy. The Minister of Defence and National Service, Hassan Rasheed, took office on 15 April 2026.
milops.source: mndf.gov.mv; Wikipedia (Ministry of Defence and National Service, Apr 2026)

milops.label: MNDF regional headquarters at Gan (Addu Atoll) and Kadhdhoo (Laamu Atoll)
milops.text: MNDF regional headquarters are at Gan (S. Gan, Addu Atoll) and Kadhdhoo (L. Kadhdhoo, Laamu Atoll). Coast Guard patrol boats are stationed at the regional headquarters.

naval.label: No navy: the MNDF Coast Guard is the armed maritime force; four squadrons and a strategic reserve at Malé
naval.text: The Maldives has no navy. The MNDF Coast Guard, a separate wing since 1980, is the armed maritime force. It runs four squadrons in the southern, central and northern regions, with a strategic reserve at Malé. Its tasks include national defence and EEZ protection, and it has taken pirate ships in the EEZ, mostly from Somalia.

naval.label: No submarine base in the Maldives; the Chinese naval-related visits found were research-vessel calls (2024)
naval.text: No submarine base is listed in the Maldives in the sources reviewed. The only Chinese naval-related visits found were the 2024 research-vessel port calls described above.

air.label: MNDF Air Corps launched 15 March 2024 at Maafaru; Bayraktar TB2 drones from Turkey; counts differ
air.text: President Mohamed Muizzu launched the MNDF Air Corps at Maafaru, Noonu Atoll, on 15 March 2024, with Bayraktar TB2 drones from Turkey for maritime surveillance. Three drones were displayed at the launch; Wikipedia lists six TB2s, which is not corroborated by a second source. The command centre is at Maafaru, whose airport opened on 1 December 2019.
air.source: Atoll Times (16 Mar 2024); The Maldives Finest (2024); migflug (2026)

air.label: Planned hangars for the drones at Gan and Funadhoo (Shaviyani), announced 2024; not verified
air.text: In 2024 the government announced that hangars for the drones would be built at Gan and at Funadhoo in Shaviyani Atoll, funded from the defence budget. The status is not verified in this build.

air.label: Gan: former RAF Gan, handed over in 1976; now the Air Corps' helicopter base in the south
air.text: Gan, in Addu Atoll, was built by the Royal Navy and used as RAF Gan. The RAF left in 1976, and the government took the site over. It is now Gan International Airport and the Air Corps' helicopter base in the south.

cyber.label: National Cyber Security Agency: the national CSIRT; newly formed in 2024; 0 of 14 on incident response (2025)
cyber.text: The National Cyber Security Agency operates the national CSIRT (CERT). A World Bank mission in September 2024 found the agency newly formed, with an incident-response centre still planned. The 2025 National Cyber Security Index scores the Maldives 0 of 14 on the national incident-response criteria.
cyber.source: NCSA (hub.ncsa.gov.mv); World Bank DMADD mission (Sep 2024); eGA NCSI (Sep 2025 version)

cyber.label: ITU and a CERT readiness assessment for the NCSA after the May 2025 Global CyberDrill
cyber.text: After the May 2025 Global CyberDrill in Dubai, the ITU committed to a CERT readiness assessment for the National Cyber Security Agency.

arms.label: No nuclear power plant, nuclear storage site or nuclear plan in the sources reviewed
arms.text: The sources reviewed show no nuclear power plant, no nuclear storage site and no nuclear energy plan for the Maldives. The energy plans cover diesel, solar, waste-to-energy and an ocean-thermal study. None is plotted.

arms.label: No missile base is listed in the Maldives in the sources reviewed
arms.text: No missile base is listed in the Maldives in the sources reviewed. None is plotted.

space.label: No space-launch site is listed in the Maldives in the sources reviewed
space.text: No space-launch site is listed in the Maldives in the sources reviewed. None is plotted.

wellbeing.label: World Happiness Report 2026: the Maldives' rank not verified in this build
wellbeing.text: The annual report ranks countries for wellbeing. The Maldives' 2026 rank was not verified in this build; check the report directly.
wellbeing.source: World Happiness Report (annual); not verified in this build

darkweb.label: Ransomware claims for the Maldives are group claims, not confirmed victims
darkweb.text: The Ransomware.live feed filtered to the Maldives' country code lists claims made by groups on their own leak sites. Each claim is labelled unverified.

markers.name: Malé (capital): MNDF headquarters, Malé Commercial Harbour, Coast Guard strategic reserve
markers.note: Capital and seat of government. The MNDF headquarters, the Ministry of Defence and National Service, the Coast Guard's strategic reserve and Malé Commercial Harbour are here (MNDF; Wikipedia, 2026). Position from the Natural Earth place record.
markers.source: Natural Earth populated places; mndf.gov.mv; Wikipedia (Ministry of Defence and National Service, Apr 2026)

markers.name: Hulhumalé (reclaimed city): SEA-ME-WE 6 cable landing (Phase II)
markers.note: Reclaimed city next to Malé. The SEA-ME-WE 6 landing point is at Hulhumalé Phase II (Dhiraagu, 2024). Chinese engagement in the Phase II housing project is reported (NUS ISAS). Position approximate.

markers.name: Hithadhoo (Addu City administrative centre), Addu Atoll
markers.note: Administrative centre of Addu City in the south. Gan, the southern air station, is on the same atoll. Position approximate.

markers.name: Eydhafushi (Baa Atoll administrative centre)
markers.note: Administrative centre of Baa Atoll (public reference). Position approximate.

markers.name: Kulhudhuffushi (Haa Dhaalu administrative centre; small domestic airport VRBK)
markers.note: Administrative centre of Haa Dhaalu Atoll. Its airport (VRBK) is a small domestic airfield (OurAirports). Position from the airport record.

markers.name: Fuvahmulah (Gnaviyani Atoll island; airport VRMF)
markers.note: Island of Gnaviyani Atoll in the south. Its airport (VRMF) is a small domestic airfield. Position from the airport record.

markers.name: Kadhdhoo (Laamu Atoll; airport VRMK; MNDF regional headquarters)
markers.note: Laamu Atoll centre. The MNDF regional headquarters for Laamu (L. Kadhdhoo) is here (Wikipedia, 2026). Position from the airport record.

markers.name: MNDF Headquarters (Bandaarakoshi, Ameer Ahmed Magu, Malé): Defence Force headquarters
markers.note: The Maldives National Defence Force's headquarters, with the Joint Operations Centre under the Integrated Headquarters. The Ministry of Defence and National Service shares the complex (mndf.gov.mv; Wikipedia, 2026). Position approximate.
markers.source: mndf.gov.mv; Wikipedia (Ministry of Defence and National Service, Apr 2026)

markers.name: MNDF Regional Headquarters S. Gan (Addu Atoll, at Gan)
markers.note: Regional headquarters for the south, at Gan in Addu Atoll (Wikipedia, Ahmed Mohamed (general), 2026). Coast Guard patrol boats are stationed at regional headquarters. Position approximate.

markers.name: MNDF Regional Headquarters L. Kadhdhoo (Laamu Atoll)
markers.note: Regional headquarters for Laamu Atoll (Wikipedia, Ahmed Mohamed (general), 2026; military-history list 'Regional Headquarters, Kahdoo, Laamu Atoll'). Position approximate.

markers.name: MNDF Coast Guard strategic reserve (Malé)
markers.note: The Coast Guard is the armed maritime force (the Maldives has no navy). Four squadrons cover the southern, central and northern regions; their positions are not published in the sources reviewed, so they are not plotted. The strategic reserve is at Malé (Wikipedia, MNDF Coast Guard, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Gan International Airport (former RAF Gan, Addu Atoll): MNDF Air Corps helicopter base
markers.note: Built by the Royal Navy and used as RAF Gan. The RAF left in 1976 and the government took over the site. The MNDF Air Corps' first helicopter was based here in 2010 (migflug, 2026). Position from the airport record (VRMG).

markers.name: Maafaru (Noonu Atoll): MNDF Air Corps drone base, Bayraktar TB2 hangar and command centre
markers.note: The Air Corps was launched here on 15 March 2024. Bayraktar TB2 drones from Turkey operate from the MNDF hangar; the command centre is here (Atoll Times, Mar 2024; migflug, 2026). The airport opened on 1 December 2019. Drone counts differ between sources: three were displayed in 2024, and Wikipedia lists six (not corroborated). Position from the airport record (VRDA).
markers.source: Atoll Times (16 Mar 2024); The Maldives Finest (2024); migflug (2026)

markers.name: PLANNED MNDF air base and hangar: Funadhoo (Shaviyani Atoll), not verified
markers.note: The government announced in 2024 that hangars would be built at Gan and at Funadhoo (Shaviyani), funded from the defence budget (Edition.mv, 2024). Not verified as built in this build. Position from the airport record (FND), which is the island's airfield.
markers.source: Edition.mv (2024); not verified in this build

markers.name: Velana International Airport (Hulhulé): expansion by a Chinese contractor; new runway opened 2018
markers.note: The main international airport, on Hulhulé next to Malé. Beijing Urban Construction Group signed the 2014 expansion; a 3,400 m runway opened in 2018, with a new fuel farm and cargo terminal (CSIS AMTI, 2018). The airport itself is civil. Position from the airport record (VRMM).
markers.source: CSIS AMTI (2018): Chinese Investment in the Maldives

markers.name: Sinamalé (China–Maldives Friendship) Bridge, Malé to Hulhulé: Chinese-financed, opened 2018
markers.note: A 2 km cross-sea bridge opened in 2018 at about US$210m, financed by a Chinese government grant and an Exim Bank concessional loan, and built by a Chinese state contractor (sources name the subsidiary differently). The loan was restructured under the G20 debt-service suspension in 2020 (AidData; Wikipedia, May 2026). Position approximate (midpoint).
markers.source: AidData (China's financing record); Wikipedia (Sinamalé Bridge, May 2026)

markers.name: Chinese research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 03: port call at Thilafushi (23 February 2024)
markers.note: Permitted in January 2024 for a port call for personnel rotation and replenishment. The ship docked at Malé and at Thilafushi on 23 February 2024. The government said it would do no research in Maldivian waters (Reuters via Malay Mail, 22 Feb 2024; SCMP, 2024). Position approximate.
markers.source: Reuters via Malay Mail (22 Feb 2024); SCMP (2024)

markers.name: Makunudhoo (Haa Dhaalu): planned Chinese–Maldivian Joint Ocean Observation Station (2017; reported scrapped; not verified)
markers.note: A 2017 protocol between China's State Oceanic Administration and the Maldives' environment ministry planned a joint ocean observation station on Makunudhoo, the westernmost inhabited island. Reports say it was scrapped (Wikipedia gives 2019). Not verified as built or dropped in this build. Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Joint Ocean Observation Station; Makunudhoo); not verified in this build

markers.name: SEA-ME-WE 6 cable landing at Hulhumalé Phase II (Dhiraagu; inaugurated 1 August 2024)
markers.note: The cable is 19,200 km long with at least 100 Tbps capacity; Dhiraagu is the first Maldivian co-owner of a global consortium of 16 partners. Full service was expected in early 2026; the go-live is not verified in this build (Dhiraagu, Aug 2024; Submarine Networks, Aug 2024). Position approximate.

markers.name: Greater Malé water supply: desalination and storage (MWSC)
markers.note: Greater Malé produces about 49,900 tonnes of water a day and holds about 50,445 tonnes in storage; a 10,000-tonne tank was added at Hulhumalé (The Standard Maldives, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: K. Funadhoo (Kaafu Atoll) fuel storage: relocation to Maagiri Falhu planned (2023; status not verified)
markers.note: The government announced in 2023 that the fuel storage at K. Funadhoo (Kaafu) would move to Maagiri Falhu, near Thilafushi (Edition.mv, 2023). The 2026 status is not verified in this build. Position approximate; the island's exact coordinates were not in the sources reviewed.
markers.source: Edition.mv (2023); not verified in this build

markers.name: Thilafushi waste-to-energy: 13 MW biopower (planned; permitting stage)
markers.note: A 13 MW waste-to-energy plant on the Thilafushi landfill and industrial island was at the permitting stage; construction was expected in 2026 and operation in 2027 (GlobalData profile, via power-technology). Not verified as built. Position approximate.

markers.name: Malé Commercial Harbour (Maldives Ports Limited): the sole port authority
markers.note: Maldives Ports Limited is the state port authority and runs Malé Commercial Harbour (Wikipedia). Its commercial operations are being relocated to Thilafushi (below). Position approximate.

markers.name: Thilafushi commercial port (relocation of Malé port operations; about 60 ha; under construction)
markers.note: Maldives Ports Limited is relocating Malé's commercial port operations to Thilafushi, on about 60 ha; the quay-wall work was targeted for July 2026 (Ministry of Economic Development, Transport and Trade, Aug 2026). Debt-financed; the source does not name the lender. Position approximate.
markers.source: Ministry of Economic Development, Transport and Trade (Aug 2026); Maldives Business Review (phase 1)

markers.name: National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA): national CSIRT and CERT
markers.note: Operates the national CSIRT (CERT) and coordinates incident response; CEO Dr Ahmed Naufal Abdul Hady (World Bank mission, Sep 2024). The office address is not published in the sources reviewed; the position is approximate (Malé). The 2025 NCSI scores incident-response capacity 0 of 14.
markers.source: NCSA (hub.ncsa.gov.mv); World Bank DMADD mission (Sep 2024); eGA NCSI (2025)

markers.name: Eight Degree Channel: sea passage at the northern edge of the archipelago (general navigation; not verified)
markers.note: A sea passage named for its latitude at the northern edge of the Maldives. General navigation reference; not verified in this build. Position approximate.
markers.source: Public information (not verified in this build)
